newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard moves assets to bond-index fund.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard moves assets to bond-index fund.

text.p: Acknowledging in part the difficulty of beating various market indices, Vanguard Group Inc said Monday it has moved fixed-income mutual fund assets in four of its Vanguard Life Strategy Portfolio "fund of funds" to a bond-index fund from a variety of bond funds.
Vanguard moved about $537 million into the Total Bond Market Portfolio of the Vanguard Bond Index Fund.
The assets were moved from the Fixed GNMA Portfolio, Fixed Short Term Corporate, Fixed Intermediate-Term Corporate, and Fixed Long-Term Corporate.

It said it completed the changes within the last week, deciding to put "greater emphasis on index investing," explaining that "over the long term it's difficult to beat indexes," according to spokesman Brian Mattes.
Mattes said the re-allocation also "marginally lowers" the expense ratios for the funds and simplifies portfolio management.
Mattes said the reshuffling occurred after the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission relaxed rules on the percentage that a fund could hold of another fund.
The Life Strategy funds include four funds -- Growth, Moderate Growth, Conservative and Income, which hold various mixes of stocks and bonds.
A fund of fund invests in other mutual funds rather than in individual securities.
